summary: A local industry’s payroll changes after a law takes effect, giving people a concrete effect to discuss.
realLife: Researchers studying Seattle’s minimum wage used Washington wage and hours records. Their estimate for restaurant employment across pay levels was close to zero even as they estimated a payroll decline for low-wage jobs across industries.
inGame: needs: a played payroll-attribution read. dev-law-industries compares business and industry figures under the changed law.
gates: The industry operates there and a payroll effect is supported.

turns.what: The employer closes the first pay period under the law with payroll level.
turns.pulledBy: Hours and staffing at that establishment have held steady.
turns.writesBack: The industry record shows the unchanged payroll for that period.

turns.what: The diner still lists the same cooks on Friday’s payroll, but one of them has lost the closing shift.
turns.pulledBy: The time sheets show fewer hours for that cook and the roster still includes everyone from the last pay period.
turns.writesBack: The district office records the lost shift under hours worked and leaves the diner’s headcount unchanged.
